method: built-in image_gen; one new generation per direction; five outputs

scope_contract.request: Five direct image deliverables plus explanation; no HTML
shared_invariants: 祈求/来源/回应/提交同屏
入口不重复，主区总览与同级子页
凡人的认知不等于神自身的体验

limitations: 所有图片是生成式视觉提案而非引擎截图

common_prompt:
Create ONE polished, original full-screen visual direction for a desktop eldritch-god turn-based simulation game. This is a complete GAME SCREEN proposal with a richly realized world and integrated, highly readable Simplified Chinese UI, not a poster, not a website, not a control dashboard. Landscape 16:9 composition, preferably 2400x1350, front-on screen view, no device mockup. The image is one of FIVE deliberately different art directions; make this one coherent and distinctive.

SHARED REAL GAME SITUATION (keep unchanged):
Turn 4, action phase. World display name "盐梦诸邦 · 001". Existing cult display name "盐梦诸邦 · 001的教团", with "信众 6" and "凝聚 60". This is a temporary existing display name; invent no other cult name. There is one cult and no relic.
Current prayer "请回应我们的祭日". Petitioner "求告的祭司 · 00000001", a LOCAL RITUAL PRIEST, NOT a member/leader of the existing cult and NOT yet known to consciously worship the player. Depict this priest conducting a local community's ritual, not directing a known congregation of the player's cult. The existing cult is a separate modest information tag. Deadline "期限：第6轮". Resource header: "第4轮" "低语 3" "信仰 6/70" "苏醒 10".
Response choices "浅触" and "深应", with shallow selected. Concise correct shallow information: "成功：留下仪式见证" and "必付：当地察觉 +2". A clearly visible primary button "以浅触回应" directly beside the choices and the information, always in the same screen. Show "本轮可回应一次". Do not invent probabilities, extra costs, automatic success, deceased people, quest rewards or a new turn mechanic. No miracle has yet been executed.
Persistent quiet access to "总览" "世界" "人物" "教团" "圣物" "本体", once each. One "结束回合" control, only once. A quiet "编年史" access. Bottom power rail with all twelve names in stable order: "聆听 入梦 谕言 赐予 任命 献祭 穿隙 播种 锚定 掩迹 迁引 降临". Later powers can be visually subdued; avoid invented lock numbers. No duplicate navigation, deep breadcrumbs or tables of backend data.

SHARED WORLD ART DIRECTION (original visual interpretation, not new game rules):
A salt-white civic settlement, everyday dwellings, locally meaningful ritual architecture, calendrical objects and worn clothing. The local ritual priest is a small human figure at a public ceremonial site; several tiny ordinary inhabitants give the civilization life. No giant character portraits. Concrete worldly reality should dominate the illustration. One faint impossible relationship of THREE OFFSET INCOMPLETE ARCS is a candidate shared divine motif, translated through local ritual forms; do NOT draw an obvious universal god-logo, a giant deity, Cthulhu face, generic tentacle border, or a literal divine avatar. The supernatural is a calm, subtle perceptual quality at the scene's edge, not a loud horror attack or an already successful miracle. The player views the known scene from outside its scale.
World image and prayer/action are both substantial. Keep main artwork ~55-65% of the useful central area, prayer identity/choices/consequences ~25-32%; integrate rather than cover the entire artwork with boxes. The scene can meet the text area through a soft shaped boundary. All Chinese labels should be sharply typeset, generous size, correct characters and breathing room. Dark-on-light or light-on-dark solid reading surfaces. Avoid decorative noise behind text. State and interaction must remain clear. The two response choices, all prayer information and submit button are simultaneously visible. No forced right-side empty column. Use the named direction-specific visual layout below; preserve information relationships but do not replicate a gray prototype's rectangles. No concept-board arrows, no multiple screens, no side-by-side variants, no other games' logos.

Small existing cult tag at left, no illustrated cult logo pretending to be a known deity. Strong graphic identity, instantly distinguishable from generic fantasy UI, while the lived world remains specific and inviting to inspect.

variants.generation_prompt:
Create ONE polished, original full-screen visual direction for a desktop eldritch-god turn-based simulation game. This is a complete GAME SCREEN proposal with a richly realized world and integrated, highly readable Simplified Chinese UI, not a poster, not a website, not a control dashboard. Landscape 16:9 composition, preferably 2400x1350, front-on screen view, no device mockup. The image is one of FIVE deliberately different art directions; make this one coherent and distinctive.

SHARED REAL GAME SITUATION (keep unchanged):
Turn 4, action phase. World display name "盐梦诸邦 · 001". Existing cult display name "盐梦诸邦 · 001的教团", with "信众 6" and "凝聚 60". This is a temporary existing display name; invent no other cult name. There is one cult and no relic.
Current prayer "请回应我们的祭日". Petitioner "求告的祭司 · 00000001", a LOCAL RITUAL PRIEST, NOT a member/leader of the existing cult and NOT yet known to consciously worship the player. Depict this priest conducting a local community's ritual, not directing a known congregation of the player's cult. The existing cult is a separate modest information tag. Deadline "期限：第6轮". Resource header: "第4轮" "低语 3" "信仰 6/70" "苏醒 10".
Response choices "浅触" and "深应", with shallow selected. Concise correct shallow information: "成功：留下仪式见证" and "必付：当地察觉 +2". A clearly visible primary button "以浅触回应" directly beside the choices and the information, always in the same screen. Show "本轮可回应一次". Do not invent probabilities, extra costs, automatic success, deceased people, quest rewards or a new turn mechanic. No miracle has yet been executed.
Persistent quiet access to "总览" "世界" "人物" "教团" "圣物" "本体", once each. One "结束回合" control, only once. A quiet "编年史" access. Bottom power rail with all twelve names in stable order: "聆听 入梦 谕言 赐予 任命 献祭 穿隙 播种 锚定 掩迹 迁引 降临". Later powers can be visually subdued; avoid invented lock numbers. No duplicate navigation, deep breadcrumbs or tables of backend data.

SHARED WORLD ART DIRECTION (original visual interpretation, not new game rules):
A salt-white civic settlement, everyday dwellings, locally meaningful ritual architecture, calendrical objects and worn clothing. The local ritual priest is a small human figure at a public ceremonial site; several tiny ordinary inhabitants give the civilization life. No giant character portraits. Concrete worldly reality should dominate the illustration. One faint impossible relationship of THREE OFFSET INCOMPLETE ARCS is a candidate shared divine motif, translated through local ritual forms; do NOT draw an obvious universal god-logo, a giant deity, Cthulhu face, generic tentacle border, or a literal divine avatar. The supernatural is a calm, subtle perceptual quality at the scene's edge, not a loud horror attack or an already successful miracle. The player views the known scene from outside its scale.
World image and prayer/action are both substantial. Keep main artwork ~55-65% of the useful central area, prayer identity/choices/consequences ~25-32%; integrate rather than cover the entire artwork with boxes. The scene can meet the text area through a soft shaped boundary. All Chinese labels should be sharply typeset, generous size, correct characters and breathing room. Dark-on-light or light-on-dark solid reading surfaces. Avoid decorative noise behind text. State and interaction must remain clear. The two response choices, all prayer information and submit button are simultaneously visible. No forced right-side empty column. Use the named direction-specific visual layout below; preserve information relationships but do not replicate a gray prototype's rectangles. No concept-board arrows, no multiple screens, no side-by-side variants, no other games' logos.

DIRECTION E — ADULT NARRATIVE TAPESTRY. A rich, uncanny textile civilization in woven linen, fine embroidery, layered felt and subtly lustrous thread. Aubergine, muted brick, flax ivory, blue-gray and restrained oxidized silver. Not cute wool toys, not a nursery craft, not a medieval medieval-book screen. Dense small woven human figures, salt-white terraces, calendrical ritual objects and everyday dwellings form one continuous panoramic cloth landscape. Near the local priest, weave is precise enough to see garments and objects; farther away it thins into sparse meaningful threads, suggesting distant perception. One restrained group of three incomplete loops in the weave quietly expresses a shared divine motif. No literal god or giant eyes. The world's inhabitants live inside this cloth-like reality naturally.
COMPOSITION: a draped but mostly frontal, expansive tapestry of the salt city occupies left and upper center. Prayer reading area on the right is an unpatterned flax-colored patch continuous with the tapestry margin, perfectly flat and screen-facing; all Chinese text is crisply typeset in dark plum, NOT laboriously stitched and not distorted. A fine stitched boundary guides the eye from the source priest to the prayer title without a visible connector graph. The two responses are understated flat cloth bands, selected one dark aubergine; the submit control is a clear wide brick-red band. Top stats and bottom twelve powers sit on smooth textile selvedges with precise readable labels. A few loose fibers on the perimeter, never over text. This should feel like the god perceives how a civilization has woven its interpretation of reality, with readable game controls and a very distinctive tactile identity.
